deities: Shri Visa Yantra (the object of worship — no idol)

history.dynasty: Nagar Brahmins (7th c. origins); Idar State rulers (13th-c. rebuild); Shri Arasuri Ambaji Mata Devasthan Trust from 1963
history.period: origins c. 7th century CE (legend claims pre-Vedic); recorded repairs 1584 and 1762; renovation 1975
history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas — venerated as the Hridaya Peetha, the spot where Sati's heart fell. There is no idol in the sanctum: the Shri Visa Yantra, a sacred-geometry diagram in a gokh (niche), is worshipped as the goddess. The present white-marble temple with gold-plated shikhara was begun c. 7th century by Nagar Brahmins, damaged by raiders in the 13th century and rebuilt by the rulers of Idar State, repaired again in 1584 and 1762; the Devasthan Trust has managed it since 1963. The original seat of the goddess is on Gabbar Hill, ~4.5 km away (see seq 1501). Legend: the King of Danta coaxed the goddess down the hill; she halted at the present site when he looked back. name: Ambaji Temple (Arasuri Ambaji Mandir)
town_description: Ambaji is a major pilgrim town in Banaskantha district in northern Gujarat, on the Gujarat–Rajasthan border at the foothills of the Arasur (southern Aravalli) hills, near the traditional source of the Saraswati river. About 180 km from Ahmedabad and 45 km from Abu Road, it draws millions of pilgrims every year, especially on Purnima (full-moon) days, and is one of Gujarat's most important Shakti Peetha towns.
